title: Tightening it with the simulator: qd-photon-sim, its evidence discipline, and the verdict

slides.title: Tightening it with the simulator
slides.subtitle: Evidence discipline, design cards, and a conditional room-temperature verdict
slides.notes: This final section turns the earlier physical ingredients into an auditable prediction. The point is not to make a simulator sound authoritative merely because it has many modules. Instead, each number enters with a provenance class, each published comparison is kept distinct from a prediction, and the sweep has explicit flux, photon-statistics, and evidence gates. We will move from architecture to material and dot models, then through electrical, spectral, phonon, and waveguide calculations. Finally we will read the acceptance sweep at its stated convention. The conclusion is deliberately conditional: the current model has useful favourable corners at non-cryogenic heat-sink temperatures, but its room-temperature linewidth and primary-platform anchors are not measurements. That distinction matters for experimental planning and for intellectual honesty. The methodology follows the repository contract and the quantum-treatment digest, which separately identify what the code computes and what remains a future quantum-optical treatment [docs/rt_edge_contract.md] [.workers/briefs/digest-qd-quantum-treatment.md].

slides.title: Architecture map: evidence-bearing modules
bullets: Materials, confinement, linewidth, and transport supply physical inputs.
Spectral, loading, phonon, and CW engines calculate observables.
Waveguide and device assemble brightness without changing intrinsic gÂ².
Cards declare assumptions; run_rt_edge executes the acceptance sweep.
Every scalar carries [V], [DR], [E], or [A] provenance.
Verification uses numbers the code did not produce.

figure.caption: Repository module flow from material inputs to the sweep verdict.

slides.notes: The map is intentionally a flow of claims rather than a black box. materials supplies parameterized III-V properties; dot_levels converts those and geometry into separable confinement and retention parameters; linewidth supplies anchored broadening; and transport accounts for the electrical route. qd_gf supplies the stationary independent-boson lineshape, spectral and loading turn filtering and occupancy into pulsed statistics, cw_g2 supplies a rate-equation regression calculation, and waveguide supplies collection. device is the integration point; cards make a design inspectable; run_rt_edge performs the grid and writes the verdict. Tags mean verified literature value [V], derived quantity [DR], class estimate [E], or declared assumption [A]. Crucially, a verifier must compare against a published number the code did not generate; otherwise agreement can be tautological. That discipline is enforced across the repositoryâ€™s verify scripts and evidence ledger [docs/rt_edge_contract.md] [fsim_core/device.py].

slides.title: Three meanings of â€œquantumâ€â€”and this modelâ€™s location

columns.heading: Device and dot
bullets: Device: confined carriers and Coulomb physics.
Dot: states and excitonâ€“bath interactions.
Simulator: separable levels plus semiclassical cascade.

columns.heading: Light
bullets: CW rates use quantum-regression identities.
No quantized optical modes or coherences.
No HOM indistinguishability prediction.

slides.notes: The ownerâ€™s slides distinguish a quantum device, a quantum treatment of the dot, and a quantum treatment of light. This simulator spans the first two only partially: confinement is quantum mechanical, and qd_gf contains a stationary excitonâ€“phonon treatment. Its primary pulsed statistic is nonetheless a level-two semiclassical cascade identity: filter leakage sets the biexciton-to-exciton ratio. For CW operation, cw_g2 solves a Markovian ladder and applies the regression construction to its rate generator. That is useful for an antibunching diagnostic, but it is not a driven Lindblad theory of quantized electromagnetic modes. In particular, it does not compute coherence-sensitive indistinguishability or a field-mode master equation. Slides three, eight, and nine of the ownerâ€™s treatment explicitly require those distinctions, so the deck labels them as absences rather than silently implying them [digest-qd-quantum-treatment.md, slides 3, 8, 9] [fsim_core/cw_g2.py].

slides.title: Materials database: platform decisions begin here
bullets: Vurgaftman parameters feed temperature-dependent III-V bands.
Strain and offsets define wells and barriers.
Critical thickness flags plausible heterostructures.
Indices feed waveguide confinement and facet extraction.
Primary: InP/GaAsP; fallback: InP/(Al)GaInP.
slides.notes: The materials layer is deliberately mundane but foundational. It provides Vurgaftman-style binary and alloy quantities, temperature-dependent band gaps, lattice mismatch, deformation-potential strain shifts, offsets, critical-thickness estimates, and refractive indices. These are not decorations: the same material choice reaches dot confinement, thermal escape, transition tracking, and guided-mode extraction. The primary card is an InP/GaAsP proposal; the fallback is an InP/(Al)GaInP, Reischle-class route. They should not be conflated. The contract records that the GaAsP solver wavelength is a known deviation from the published short-wavelength class, and calls for a direct platform measurement. This is why a database value is tagged with its source class, and why the platform choice is a conditional design decision rather than a measured device claim [Vurgaftman et al., JAP 89, 5815 (2001)] [fsim_core/materials.py] [docs/rt_edge_contract.md].

slides.title: Dot levels: useful retention parameters, explicit deviations
bullets: Separable cylindrical solver estimates electron and hole levels.
It hands activation energies and prefactors to device retention.
It reproduces confinement-scale trends, not full multiband strain.
Piezoelectric fields and true three-dimensional relaxation are omitted.
slides.notes: dot_levels is a separable finite-disk effective-mass solver, so its value is traceability and fast sensitivity analysis, not a claim to replace multiband kÂ·p. It derives confinement levels and then converts their escape separations into the two-channel retention parameters passed forward: activation energies, escape prefactors, and the power-law channel. The verification output compares its results with Chatzarakis-class wetting-layer separations and Reischle-class line ranges. The deviations table is as important as the matches: flat-band cylindrical confinement omits piezoelectric fields, true three-dimensional strain relaxation, and band mixing, so piezoelectric structures can disagree substantially. The module documents those limits beside the calculations. Retention is therefore a model-derived bridge, and each design card must retain its [E] or [A] label rather than presenting it as a direct measurement [verify/verify_dot_levels.py] [Chatzarakis et al., Phys. Rev. Applied 20, 034011 (2023)] [Reischle et al., Opt. Express 16, 12771 (2008)].

slides.title: Linewidth: anchored where measured, conditional where not
bullets: Anchors include the narrow and broad class endpoints.
The InP-dot room-temperature width remains unmeasured.
Sweep linewidth is therefore an [E] sensitivity axis.
Measurement 1 must resolve Î“(T) on InP/GaAsP.
slides.notes: The linewidth model makes a disciplined distinction between anchor data and the target platform. Its parameterization is anchored by a narrow class proxy from Chatzarakis and a broader class proxy from Matsuda, then evaluated as a temperature trend. Neither is a direct linewidth measurement of a single InP/GaAsP dot at room temperature. The contract therefore labels gamma300 as an estimate and sweeps it instead of treating it as settled. This has immediate consequence: the headline gate can clear at a sufficiently narrow sampled linewidth, but that is not evidence that a fabricated InP/GaAsP device will have that linewidth. The ownerâ€™s first measurement is precisely the missing distribution of biexciton splitting and Î“(T) on this platform. Until that experiment exists, the correct conclusion is conditional. The anchors are still valuable as bounded class information, provided their material mismatch is never hidden [fsim_core/linewidth.py] [Chatzarakis 2023 PRA 20 034011] [Matsuda et al., PRB 63, 121304(R) (2001)].

slides.title: Electrical model: the Section 3 stack in one slide
bullets: Two-diode Iâ€“V uses aperture-area current density.
Injection efficiency and quasi-Fermi suppression shape capture.
Carrier budget assigns a per-dot share and cap-two loading.
Urbach tail plus residual background sets spectral impurity.
Junction temperature is solved self-consistently.
slides.notes: This slide is a bridge back to the electrical detail of Section 3. transport evaluates a two-diode current-voltage law at the actual aperture area, rather than confusing total current with current density. Injection and capture efficiency then feed a carrier budget, including a statistically meaningful per-dot share and a cap-two occupancy construction. The model distinguishes suppression at the dot energy from suppression at background energies through quasi-Fermi factors. An Urbach tail and a residual background supply the spectral impurity that mixes with the desired line. Finally, heating is not merely appended afterward: junction temperature is part of the evaluation loop, so every thermal quantity sees the operating condition. This remains a macroscopic transport model, however; it does not dynamically couple drift-diffusion carrier fields to a quantum density matrix. That missing Kantner-style closure returns on the final roadmap slide [fsim_core/transport.py] [fsim_core/device.py] [Sze & Ng, Physics of Semiconductor Devices, 3rd ed.].

slides.title: Spectral engine: cascade leakage, loading, and temperature ceiling

equations.caption: signal fraction rho; filtered XX and X transmissions t_XX and t_X
loading Fano factor F_p and mean occupancy mu

slides.notes: The F-series identities make the modelâ€™s pulsed statistic inspectable. First, a background mixture transforms dot statistics by the squared signal fraction rho. Second, in the weak-pump filtered cascade, the residual central peak is the ratio of biexciton and exciton transmission. loading adds a Fano-parameterized occupancy correction with cap-two logic. The ownerâ€™s slide eight places the lower leakage bound, loading Fano factor, and crossing-temperature definition together; the repository distributes them across spectral.epsilon2, loading.f1b_g2 and f8_g2_load, and device.evaluate. This distribution is not a conceptual gap, but it is a reason to cite the functions rather than describe an anonymous â€œengine.â€ These formulas are powerful because every term is diagnosable. They are also limited: their pulsed result is not an optical-field Lindblad simulation. The lecture therefore treats them as semiclassical identities with stated conditions [fsim_core/spectral.py] [fsim_core/loading.py] [fsim_core/device.py] [Reischle et al., Opt. Express 16, 12771 (2008), Eq. 1].

slides.title: CW engine: regression, IRF, and the low-pump diagnostic
slides.notes: The CW module treats the empty, exciton, and biexciton populations as a Markovian rate ladder. It obtains the conditional intensity through the rate-equation regression construction, reports the low-pump closed-form limit, and then mixes signal and background pointwise. Detector response is a separate convolution step, including the two-sided-exponential erfcx dip formula used to reproduce the Reischle-style instrument broadening and its inverse deconvolution convention. This separation is pedagogically useful: an intrinsic dip, a background-included dip, and a raw IRF-broadened dip are different reported quantities, and comparing unlike conventions is a category error. The acceptance sweep uses CW values as diagnostics, while the headline pulsed gate remains intrinsic and background-included by its defined convention. The moduleâ€™s regression language should not be overread as a quantized-light solution: it operates on a rate generator without optical coherences [fsim_core/cw_g2.py] [Reischle et al., Optics Express 16, 12771 (2008)].

slides.title: Phonons: independent-boson lineshape, not driven polaron dynamics
bullets: qd_gf models LA deformation-potential coupling.
It returns a ZPL plus phonon sideband spectrum.
Piezoelectric and LO couplings remain absent.
Driven polaron renormalisation remains future work.
slides.notes: qd_gf implements the independent-boson model for a stationary two-level exciton coupled diagonally to bulk longitudinal-acoustic phonons through deformation potential. It constructs a spectral density, Huangâ€“Rhys weight, zero-phonon line, phonon sideband, and sideband-aware filter transmission. That is a meaningful improvement over a bare Lorentzian, but its scope is deliberately narrow. It does not include piezoelectric coupling, optical LO coupling, or a polaron-frame driven Hamiltonian whose Rabi frequency is renormalized during excitation. Nor does it provide phonon-assisted transitions in the electrical pulse dynamics. These omissions matter especially near the intended high-temperature regime; they are not small implementation details to hide beneath an â€œIBMâ€ label. The ownerâ€™s gap list names exactly these extensions. Keeping the stationary result and the driven open-system problem separate makes the present predictions more, not less, useful [fsim_core/qd_gf.py] [Krummheuer et al., PRB 65, 195313 (2002)] [Nazir & McCutcheon, JPCM 28, 103002 (2016)].

slides.title: Waveguide collection: brightness lever, never a gÂ² lever

equations.caption: linear collection efficiency eta cancels from normalized coincidence

bullets: beta, facets, propagation, and NA determine collected flux.
Lemma 1 forbids collection from improving intrinsic gÂ².
Verification tests this invariance explicitly.
slides.notes: The edge-waveguide model supplies beta coupling, propagation, facet behavior, and numerical-aperture collection. All of these can be decisive for whether a photon rate is measurable, but none can repair the intrinsic multiphoton probability. Lemma 1 is just linear-loss invariance: a passive collection channel thins singles and coincidences by the same appropriate powers, which cancel in normalized g2. The contract elevates this simple fact into a testable rule because it prevents a common reporting mistake: claiming an optical collection upgrade improved source purity. It can improve observed count rate, signal-to-background conditions if background has a different optical path, or experimental feasibility; it cannot change the dotâ€™s intrinsic correlation through ordinary linear loss. The waveguide and device verifiers exercise this separation, so a code change that leaks collection into the wrong g2 term is caught. This is a conceptual guardrail as much as a numerical result [docs/rt_edge_contract.md] [verify/verify_waveguide.py] [fsim_core/waveguide.py].

slides.title: Contract and evidence ledger: claims must survive adversarial checking
bullets: Two independent sources are required per central claim.
DOIs and locators make each value inspectable.
Digest cross-checks reject value-level mutations.
Fabricated anchors must fail, not merely look cited.
Ledger status: 14/17 checks; three claims remain single-source.
slides.notes: The contract turns literature citation into a testable interface. A central claim needs two independent sources, with DOI and locator information, and the local digest is independently cross-checked against the claimed value. The verification suite also deliberately mutates a real value and tries fabricated-anchor scenarios; a credible ledger must reject both. The current evidence state is incomplete: fourteen of seventeen paper checks pass, while three central items remain single-sourced. The tier document names the important gaps: no second verified electrical single-dot comparison at the eighty-kelvin anchor, an unreproduced primary-platform wavelength, and a transferred residual-background claim. These failures are not cosmetic bibliography issues: the contract says they independently block an unconditional PASS. This approach makes a negative result informative, because it localizes whether the limit is physics, flux eligibility, or evidence [out/rt_edge/evidence.json] [docs/rt_edge_contract.md] [docs/rt_edge_tier.md].

columns.heading: Primary
bullets: edge-inp-gaasp-design
InP/GaAsP target platform
Requires platform-specific measurement.

columns.heading: Fallback
bullets: edge-inp-gainp-design
InP/(Al)GaInP Reischle-class route
Favourable sweep operating point.

slides.notes: Design cards are not just parameter files. They are the place where every scalar must name its provenance, range, and whether it is verified, derived, estimated, or assumed. The primary card represents the intended InP/GaAsP platform, while the fallback card represents an InP/(Al)GaInP route closer to the Reischle material class. Each includes dot, drive, optical collection, and thermal operating information. The sweep does not erase the distinction: it records per-card eligibility and diagnostics, and the contract explains why a good fallback corner cannot validate the unmeasured primary platform. This card discipline makes it possible to ask a constructive question after any adverse result: which exact scalar is the next measurement, and which is merely a knob? It also prevents copied â€œtypicalâ€ numbers from becoming silent facts. The cards should be read as structured hypotheses with citations, not fabrication-ready specifications [cards/edge-inp-gaasp-design.yaml] [cards/edge-inp-gainp-design.yaml] [docs/rt_edge_contract.md].

slides.title: Acceptance sweep: gates, axes, and verdict
bullets: Axes: Î”XX, Î“300, IRF, NA, Rback, length, and heat-sink temperature.
Eligibility requires the collected-flux floor.
Headline gate: pulsed intrinsic gÂ² below one half.
CW values are diagnostics; evidence is an independent gate.
slides.notes: The acceptance sweep is designed to make tradeoffs visible. It spans biexciton splitting, room-temperature linewidth, detector response, numerical aperture, back reflectivity, cavity length, and heat-sink temperature. A row must first satisfy the collected-flux floor to be eligible. The headline gate is pulsed intrinsic g2 below one half under the specified background convention. CW correlations remain diagnostics rather than a second hidden headline. Finally, the evidence gate prevents a numerical corner from being declared an established device. The printed verdict is intentionally dense because it identifies the aggregate statistics, eligibility denominator, coverage convention, linewidth bracket, and temperature-resolved coverage. Its first word is FAIL: the median and evidence gates are not met, even though individual favourable rows pass the pulsed statistic. The appropriate reading is conditional design guidance, not a claim of room-temperature electrical demonstration [out/rt_edge/verdict.md] [docs/rt_edge_contract.md]. Exact sweep line: VERDICT: FAIL g2_min=0.3214 g2_median_eligible=0.6373 diag_g2_min=0.3214 diag_g2_median_diagnostic=0.6706 flux_max=6890 flux_margin=6.89 flux_shortfall_deprecated=0.1451 median_pass=false coverage_over_eligible=0.3066 eligible_fraction=0.5521 eligible=424/768 flux_floor_excluded=344 evidence=incomplete conditional=true headline_coverage=130/768 cw_raw_coverage=0/424 gamma300_pass_max=10 gamma300_threshold=10-12 T_pass_min=230 headline_by_T=230:60/192,250:34/192,273:24/192,300:12/192

slides.notes: The temperature table is the most direct answer to â€œwhat does cooling buy?â€ At the lowest non-cryogenic heat-sink slice, more rows are flux eligible and more clear the pulsed headline gate. As the heat sink warms, flux eligibility falls and the favourable minimum rises, although individual sampled corners remain below the headline threshold even at the warmest slice. The linewidth threshold information must be read as a sampled bracket, not a continuous fit: it identifies where the grid changes classification. The reported minimum passing heat-sink temperature is the lowest scheduled non-cryogenic slice with a passing corner, not a universal operating temperature for either platform. This plot uses the live verdict values and visualizes only the favourable boundary; it does not substitute for the full multidimensional sweep. The full CSV remains the source for lever-by-lever interpretation [out/rt_edge/verdict.md] [out/rt_edge/sweep.csv].

slides.title: What cooling buys at the favourable corner
slides.notes: Cooling changes more than one scalar, so a single intuitive explanation is insufficient. At the favourable corner, the retained carrier fraction drops as temperature rises, the linewidth broadens, and the in-window background changes with the operating model. The table places these quantities together precisely to avoid attributing the whole trend to linewidth alone. Retention is especially consequential because it enters the brightness chain multiplicatively and becomes the smallest factor at the warm end. The non-monotonic background values also warn against telling a simple â€œhotter means more backgroundâ€ story without specifying the spectral window, injection state, and thermal solution. These are evaluated sweep outputs, not independent measurements. The experimental implication is clear: cooling can buy both usable flux and spectral separation, but the room-temperature platform decision still requires direct Î“(T) and splitting measurements. The verdictâ€™s temperature table and cooling section are the authoritative numerical record [out/rt_edge/verdict.md] [fsim_core/device.py].

slides.title: Brightness chain: identify the limiter before optimizing
bullets: Loading, retention, filtering, and extraction multiply.
Waveguide levers can clear flux eligibility.
At the favourable warm corner, retention is the smallest factor.
Collection improves rate; Lemma 1 protects gÂ² accounting.
slides.notes: Brightness is not a monolithic output. The verdict decomposes it into the repetition and loading route, thermal retention, spectral transmission, and optical extraction chain. That factor table is more actionable than a final count rate because it identifies whether the next engineering intervention should be electrical, material, spectral, or optical. In the reviewed favourable corner, the dominant limiter is retention S, not the numerical aperture or facet once the collection levers are applied. This is consistent with the temperature sweep: a better lens cannot restore carriers that escape before radiative emission. Conversely, collection changes can still be essential because the acceptance protocol has a minimum measurable-flux requirement. The correct optimization order therefore uses the factor table: remove the smallest physical multiplier first, while keeping purity and collection accounting distinct. The council review specifically required the whole-chain smallest factor to be named, preventing a visually prominent optical lever from being mistaken for the fundamental bottleneck [out/rt_edge/verdict.md] [docs/rt_edge_tier.md] [fsim_core/waveguide.py].

slides.title: Validation against papers: compare conventions before numbers
bullets: Reischle: deconvolved, background-included comparison at 80 K.
Chatzarakis: temperature-trend comparison near 230 K.
Fresh card evaluation prevents stale fixture values.
Predictions are not retrospective measurements.
slides.notes: Paper validation is useful only when the reported conventions match. For Reischle, the appropriate comparison is the IRF-deconvolved but background-included value, not the raw detector-broadened dip and not the fully background-corrected value. The tier document records that anchor as 0.25 plus or minus 0.05, with roughly four kilocounts per second, and explicitly calls the model comparison a prediction. For Chatzarakis, the comparison is a temperature-trend point near 230 K rather than a claim of shared material or electrical drive. The verification route loads the current card and calls device.evaluate, avoiding a stale hard-coded result. This is the right use of literature: test units, trends, and reporting conventions while retaining material and excitation differences. A match at a proxy point does not convert an estimated InP/GaAsP room-temperature linewidth into a measurement [docs/rt_edge_tier.md] [verify/verify_rt_edge_papers.py] [Reischle et al., Optics Express 16, 12771 (2008)].

slides.title: Council review history: why a simulator earns conditional trust
bullets: Seven Opus reviews and one cross-review drove six fixes.
Reviews caught facet, threshold, and reporting-attribution errors.
They separated flux failure from physics failure.
Trust comes from reproducible criticism, not confidence language.
slides.notes: The tier history records repeated adversarial review rather than a one-pass implementation. Seven Opus passes, a codex-sol cross-review, and six fix rounds found issues in facet accounting, reporting conventions, linewidth brackets, background attribution, and the distinction between flux eligibility and a genuine physics failure. Several of those changes are deceptively small in code but decisive in interpretation: applying a facet factor twice would inflate brightness; a numeric threshold when no sampled row passes would imply unsupported physics; comparing raw and intrinsic correlations would exaggerate agreement. The review process matters because a simulatorâ€™s most dangerous errors are often not crashes. They are plausible-looking values with the wrong denominator, convention, or evidence status. By writing such objections into regression checks and the verdict text, the project makes future changes answer to the same criticism. That is the practical meaning of evidence discipline [docs/rt_edge_tier.md] [verify/verify_rt_edge_sweep.py] [verify/verify_rt_edge_papers.py].

slides.title: Honest conclusion: conditional non-cryogenic passes, no unconditional PASS
bullets: Stop rule is non-cryogenic: heat-sink temperature at least 230 K.
Individual favourable corners meet the pulsed gÂ² gate.
Aggregate verdict remains FAIL: evidence is incomplete.
Measurement 1: Î”XX distribution and Î“(T) on InP/GaAsP.
A second electrical 80 K anchor is also required.
slides.notes: The stop rule is intentionally weaker than an unqualified room-temperature claim: it asks whether a favourable design point exists at a non-cryogenic heat-sink temperature, defined here as at least 230 K. The sweep finds such corners, so the physics sensitivity exercise has a useful result. But the final verdict remains FAIL. The median gate is not met, the evidence ledger is incomplete, and the key room-temperature InP/GaAsP linewidth remains unmeasured. A PASS would require Measurement 1: a distribution of biexciton splittings and linewidth versus temperature on the primary platform, so the sensitivity axes become measured inputs. It would also require a second independent source for the electrical 80 K anchor. The distinction is not semantic. It tells an experimental team exactly what data would change the conclusion, and it keeps the deck from turning a conditional model corner into a demonstration claim [out/rt_edge/verdict.md] [docs/rt_edge_contract.md] [docs/rt_edge_tier.md].

slides.notes: The roadmap is module-specific so that â€œfuture workâ€ does not become a vague promise. A Lindblad treatment with quantized field modes and an indistinguishability observable would reach beyond cw_g2â€™s population-rate calculation and into device integration. Polaron-frame driven dynamics would couple qd_gf to the excitation model; piezoelectric and LO phonons would extend its Hamiltonian rather than merely alter a phenomenological linewidth. Kantner-style transport-to-Lindblad coupling would make carrier capture and escape dynamically bidirectional between transport and the dot density matrix. The Zhao stochastic closure would revisit the empirical Fano factor used by loading. Finally, piezoelectric fields in dot_levels would address the known flat-band confinement failure for the Chatzarakis-like structures. Each item changes a different model boundary, which is why none should be implied by the present simulations. The ownerâ€™s slide nine and gap list specify these as still to do [digest-qd-quantum-treatment.md, slide 9] [Kantner et al., PRB 96, 205301 (2017)] [Zhao et al., PRR 6, L032021 (2024)].

slides.title: Closing summary and references
bullets: Confinement, emission, driving, and photonics form one chain.
Simulator predictions are useful only with stated scope and evidence.
Favourable non-cryogenic corners guide measurements, not claims.
References: Fox; Vurgaftman; Reischle; Chatzarakis; Krummheuer; Kantner; Zhao.
slides.notes: Across the lecture, we have followed a single photon from confined carrier states through spontaneous emission and phonon coupling, photon statistics, electrical injection, and photonic extraction. The simulator unifies those elements well enough to pose design questions quantitatively, but its credibility rests on keeping levels of approximation visible. Its strongest present output is a conditional map: it identifies favourable non-cryogenic corners, the sensitivity to linewidth and splitting, the brightness bottleneck, and the measurements that could promote estimates to evidence. Its clearest negative output is equally valuable: an unconditional room-temperature electrical single-dot claim is not supported by this sweep or ledger. The sources used throughout the deck include Fox, Bimberg, Vurgaftman, Sze and Ng, Coldren, Reischle, Chatzarakis, Laferriere, Krummheuer, Nazir, Kantner, and Zhao; earlier section JSON files provide the deduplicated detailed citations. A rigorous closing message is therefore not â€œthe simulator proved it,â€ but â€œthe simulator made the next decisive experiment explicitâ€ [docs/rt_edge_contract.md] [docs/rt_edge_tier.md].
